propositions: Three independent code paths (normal compaction, fsck rebuild, crash recovery) each re-derive the same candidate listing, snapshot detection, envelope building, retire-rename logic, and commit steps with duplicated implementations.
The SNAPSHOT envelope builder and source-event-uuid generation appear in at least two places (compact_txn and compact_rebuild) with identical functionality but separate code.
The retire-rename-back logic with data-loss guards appears three times across compact_txn, compact_recovery, and rollback paths, creating maintenance burden and inconsistency risks.
A shared compact_plan module consolidates these derivations into reusable functions while preserving separate crash models (fsck's abort-and-rollback for folds vs rebuild's idempotent .bak sentinel).
The guard construction prevents future duplication of SNAPSHOT-envelope keys and retired-rename operations outside the owner module via linting rules and excusal markers.
